# Kindly kinds

[Kindly](https://scicloj.github.io/kindly-noted/) is a convention from
the Clojure ecosystem for annotating values with rendering intent.
Babqua supports Kindly [metadata](https://clojure.org/reference/metadata),
so the same code patterns work in both Babashka+Quarto and
Clojure+Clay.

Without an annotation, results display as code output:

```{.clojure .bb}
(let [people [{:name "Alice" :scores [85 92 78]}
              {:name "Bob"   :scores [91 88 95]}
              {:name "Carol" :scores [76 80 89]}]]
  (map (fn [p]
         {:name (:name p)
          :avg  (/ (apply + (:scores p)) (count (:scores p)))})
       people))
```

One exception: `(def x ...)` returns the var (`#'user/x`), which is
noise rather than information. Babqua suppresses var results by
default, so a setup block like `(def magic-number 42)` is hidden
without needing `#| output: hidden`. Reference the binding in a
later block to display its value.

Add Kindly metadata to control how a value is rendered.

## `^:kind/hiccup` — HTML from data

Converts a [hiccup](https://github.com/weavejester/hiccup) vector to
HTML. Hiccup represents HTML as nested Clojure vectors:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/hiccup
[:svg {:width "100" :height "100" :xmlns "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"}
  [:circle {:cx "50" :cy "50" :r "40" :fill "coral"}]]
```

The vector `[:tag {:attr "value"} content]` becomes
`<tag attr="value">content</tag>`. Babashka has
[hiccup2.core](https://github.com/weavejester/hiccup) built in, so the
HTML rendering happens on the Babashka side, not in the Lua filter.

## `^:kind/html` — raw HTML

Renders a string as raw HTML. Since strings can't hold metadata in
Clojure, wrap the expression in a vector:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/html
["<b>bold</b> and <em>italic</em>"]
```

The vector is automatically unwrapped — Babqua extracts the first
element for rendering.

## `^:kind/md` — markdown

Renders a string as markdown. Same wrapping rule as `kind/html`:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/md
["| a | b |\n| --- | --- |\n| 1 | 2 |"]
```

## `^:kind/hidden` — suppress output

Evaluates the code but hides the result. The code itself is still
shown. Useful for setup like defining helper functions:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/hidden
[(def my-data [1 2 3])]
```

## `^:kind/mermaid` — Mermaid diagrams

Renders a string as a [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) diagram. The
Mermaid JS library is loaded automatically from CDN:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/mermaid
["graph LR\n  A[Start] --> B{Decision}\n  B -->|Yes| C[OK]\n  B -->|No| D[Cancel]"]
```

## `^:kind/graphviz` — Graphviz diagrams

Renders a string as a [Graphviz](https://graphviz.org/) DOT diagram.
The [`viz-js`](https://github.com/mdaines/viz-js) library is loaded
from CDN; no local Graphviz install needed:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/graphviz
["digraph { rankdir=LR; A -> B -> C; A -> C; }"]
```

## `^:kind/tex` — LaTeX formulas

Renders a string as a LaTeX formula via
[MathJax](https://www.mathjax.org/):

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/tex
["\\int_0^\\infty e^{-x^2} dx = \\frac{\\sqrt{\\pi}}{2}"]
```

## `^:kind/code` — code display

Renders a string as syntax-highlighted Clojure code (for display, not
evaluation):

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/code
["(defn hello [name]\n  (str \"Hello, \" name \"!\"))"]
```

## `^:kind/vega-lite` — Vega-Lite charts

Renders a map as a [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/)
chart. The JS library is loaded automatically from CDN:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/vega-lite
{:data {:values [{:x "A" :y 28} {:x "B" :y 55} {:x "C" :y 43}]}
 :mark :bar
 :encoding {:x {:field :x :type :nominal}
            :y {:field :y :type :quantitative}}}
```

## `^:kind/plotly` — Plotly charts

Renders a map as a [Plotly.js](https://plotly.com/javascript/) chart.
The spec should have `:data` and `:layout` keys:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/plotly
{:data [{:x [1 2 3 4] :y [10 15 13 17] :type "scatter" :mode "lines+markers"}]
 :layout {:title "Simple Plotly Chart"}}
```

## `^:kind/table` — HTML tables

Renders tabular data as an HTML table. Two value shapes are accepted:

A sequence of maps (header derived from union of keys):

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/table
[{:lang "Clojure"  :year 2007}
 {:lang "Babashka" :year 2020}
 {:lang "Jank"     :year 2019}]
```

Or a column-vector form:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/table
{:column-names ["x" "x²" "x³"]
 :row-vectors  [[1 1 1]
                [2 4 8]
                [3 9 27]]}
```

The table is rendered on the Babashka side (via hiccup) and inserted
as raw HTML, so styling can target it the same way as any other HTML
table.

## Annotating in library functions

The `^:kind/...` reader syntax attaches metadata at the call site.
But metadata can also be attached programmatically with
[`with-meta`](https://clojuredocs.org/clojure.core/with-meta) or
[`vary-meta`](https://clojuredocs.org/clojure.core/vary-meta), which
means **library functions can annotate their return values**. The
caller doesn't need to know about the rendering — the function
handles it.

For example, a function that builds an SVG bar chart and tags it as
hiccup:

```{.clojure .bb}
(defn bar-chart [labels values]
  (let [bar-width 40
        gap       10
        max-val   (apply max values)
        height    120
        bars      (map-indexed
                    (fn [i [label val]]
                      (let [x          (+ 10 (* i (+ bar-width gap)))
                            bar-height (* (/ val max-val) height)]
                        [:g
                         [:rect {:x x :y (- height bar-height)
                                 :width bar-width :height bar-height
                                 :fill "steelblue"}]
                         [:text {:x (+ x (/ bar-width 2)) :y (+ height 15)
                                 :text-anchor "middle" :font-size "12"}
                          label]]))
                    (map vector labels values))
        total-width (+ 20 (* (count labels) (+ bar-width gap)))]
    (with-meta
      (into [:svg {:width total-width :height (+ height 25)
                   :xmlns "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"}] bars)
      {:kindly/kind :kind/hiccup})))
```

Now simply calling the function renders the chart — no annotation
needed at the call site:

```{.clojure .bb}
(bar-chart ["a" "b" "c"] [10 20 15])
```

This is a key idea behind Kindly: rendering intent lives in the
metadata of values, not in the document markup. Libraries can provide
visualization functions that "just work" in any Kindly-aware tool —
Babqua, Clay, Janqua, or others.

## Why wrap strings in vectors?

In Clojure (and Babashka), metadata can only be attached to
collections — vectors, maps, sets — not to primitive types like
strings or numbers. So `^:kind/html "hello"` won't work.

The convention is to wrap the value in a vector:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/html ["<b>hello</b>"]
```

Babqua automatically unwraps the vector for all string-valued kinds
(`kind/html`, `kind/md`, `kind/mermaid`, `kind/graphviz`, `kind/tex`,
`kind/code`), extracting the first element for rendering.

## Summary of kinds

| Kind | Value type | Renders as |
|:-----|:-----------|:-----------|
| `^:kind/hiccup` | vector (hiccup) | HTML |
| `^:kind/html` | `[string]` | raw HTML |
| `^:kind/md` | `[string]` | markdown |
| `^:kind/hidden` | any | nothing (evaluates silently) |
| `^:kind/mermaid` | `[string]` | Mermaid diagram |
| `^:kind/graphviz` | `[string]` | Graphviz diagram |
| `^:kind/tex` | `[string]` | LaTeX formula |
| `^:kind/code` | `[string]` | syntax-highlighted code |
| `^:kind/vega-lite` | map | Vega-Lite chart |
| `^:kind/plotly` | map | Plotly chart |
| `^:kind/echarts` | map | [ECharts](https://echarts.apache.org/) chart |
| `^:kind/cytoscape` | map | [Cytoscape](https://js.cytoscape.org/) graph |
| `^:kind/highcharts` | map | [Highcharts](https://www.highcharts.com/) chart |
| `^:kind/table` | map or seq-of-maps | HTML table |
| _(none)_ | any | code output |
